result.summary: The landlord has approved the agency instructing a contractor for the leaking bathroom tap (event 008), but I couldn't assign one because there's no plumber on record and the landlord didn't name one. Choosing a provider needs agency judgement, so it's in the operations queue (item 29) at normal priority. I emailed the tenant to say a plumber is being arranged, gave them safe steps to contain the leak and asked when they're available. A hold is set to follow up in 1 day.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 008 is a clear approval of the attendance the agency described in event 003: "agrees to have a contractor instructed". The classifier agrees (approve p=1.0, unconditional 0.84, auto). Normally the next step would be assign_contractor. But the ticket has no contractor, the property has no previous jobs and the landlord didn't name anyone. Picking a name would mean inventing one, so choosing the provider has to go to ops.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No contractor appears anywhere in the records, so any name would be made up.

alternatives_considered.option: Ask the landlord to name a contractor
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord has already handed the choice to the agency. Asking again would hold up approved work.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat it as an emergency and escalate at high priority
alternatives_considered.why_not: The leak only happens while the shower is running, so the tenant can contain it. The emergency score was only 0.57. I sent containment advice and kept the priority at normal, flagged as urgent.
Approved work would stall and the tenant would have no update.
